newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds firm, expecting no rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds firm, expecting no rate worries.

text.p: *Australian bonds closed firm in anticipation that the Federal Reserve will keep policy unchanged at next Tuesday's meeting, and there are some that see scope for a local easing.
*Close watch put on next week's final wages data.
Australian bonds closed firm in anticipation that the Federal Reserve will keep policy unchanged at next Tuesday's meeting, and some players are still looking at a possible local easing.

Futures struck 12-week highs as the participants unwound concerns over a possible tightening at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday following the recent flow of data, although analysts still saw a pre-emptive hike down the track.
While global markets will be closely watching the FOMC, locally next Thursday's final wages data will also be closely watched amid chatter about a possible easing.
A weak private sector on the wages split will likely keep the momentum of a complete outside chance of an easing on the cards, analysts said.
Bill futures have been particularly active over the past couple of sessions on an outside chance an easing, despite repeated warnings by the RBA over its wage growth concerns,
This momentum has been kept up by RBA governor Ian Macfarlane saying that the central bank will not stand in the way of growth, so long as it does not damage inflation.
However, despite this from trend, March 1998 bill futures are still perdicting a 50 basis point rate hike.

Local debt continued to show an outperforming bias against the U.S., although spreads were slightly above their initial lows. The U.S. weakened on a jump in core April CPI and a drop in jobless claims on Thursday, but rebounded on flat industrial production and a fall in capacity utilisation.
